To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the structure of the native DHQase has been solved at a resolution of 1.78 Angstroms; (b) a modified enzyme has been crystallized and its structure determined at 2.1 Angstroms; and (c) a comparison of the three crystal forms has provided new information about the dimerization and the active site of this enzyme.

(i) DHQase exists as an active dimer, (ii) the dimer interface is formed by the N-terminal helix and the loop between beta strands 3 and 4, (iii) the lid-loop is in an open position in the native enzyme but in a closed position in the modified enzyme and (iv) the active site is formed by residues from both subunits of the enzyme.

the crystal structures of the type I 3-DHQase from Salmonella Typhi, both in the apo-enzyme and the product-inhibited forms, have been determined and the structural information obtained is being used to design new inhibitors for the enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and mechanism of the 3-dehydroqinase enzyme, which catalyzes the reversible dehydration of the 3-keto acid intermediate of the shikimate biosynthetic pathway.
the structure of a type I DHQases and the implications of the crystallographic structures on the catalytic mechanism of DHQases.
the elucidation of the structural basis of enzyme activity, which will provide the necessary information for the development of new antimicrobial and herbicidal drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzyme is active only in the open conformation.
the crystallographic structure is the most important factor for the enzyme activity.

the crystallographic structure determination of the native enzyme has revealed a novel dimerization mode for DHQases, while the structure of the product-inhibited enzyme has revealed the details of the active site and the mode of binding of the inhibitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallographic studies have revealed a new crystal form of the DHQase from S. typhi which is more suitable for the co-crystallization of the enzyme-product complex.
the type I DH Qase from Salmonella Typhi has been crystallised and its structure determined.
the crystallographic structure determination of DHQase has been achieved and the structural information has been used to understand the enzyme activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single amino acid change in the active site of the DHQase enzyme from S. typhi (Glu-166 to Asp) results in a 10-fold increase in the k(cat) and a 100-fold increase in the K(m) of the enzyme.
the crystal form in which the product has covalently attached to the active site residue is a better model for the enzyme-substrate complex.
the enzyme can function in two distinct crystal forms.
